Timeline

Events in the order they happened, each with its time, who acted and what happened, joined by a rail.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For the history of one run, task or approval: who did what, and when.
  • For a run in progress, with the step it is on now marked as the current one.
  • With the dense variant for a long log of short events.

When not to use it

  • For the messages of a conversation with an agent. Use message rows in a transcript.
  • For steps the reader has yet to take, such as a setup wizard. This component records what happened.
  • For a set of things in no particular order. Use the list.
  • For events compared across columns, or filtered and sorted. Use the data table.
  • When there are no events, while the first fetch runs or after it fails. Put an empty state, a spinner or an error state in place of the list. Never render an ol with no items.

Variants

default
Time and actor on one line, what happened on the next, 16px between events.
dense ds-timeline--dense
8px between events, with what happened on the same line as the time and actor where there is room.

Accessibility

  • Use an ol with one li, ds-timeline__item, for each event, oldest first unless the view says otherwise. A screen reader announces the count and the position.
  • Each item holds a p with the class ds-timeline__meta and then a p with the class ds-timeline__event. The meta line holds a time element, ds-timeline__time, with a datetime attribute, and the actor, ds-timeline__actor, in words. The event line says what happened as a sentence fragment that starts with a verb.
  • Write the time so it cannot be misread: the clock time for events of one day, the date as well when the list spans days.
  • Mark the current step with aria-current="step" on its li and with words in a span of the class ds-timeline__current at the end of the meta line, such as Current step. The filled mark only supports the words.
  • The rail and the marks are drawn by the stylesheet and are decoration. Nothing is said by them alone.
  • A long timeline pairs with show-more: render the most recent events, twenty or so, and put one secondary button after the list whose label gives the count, such as Show 34 earlier events. On press the app adds the items to the same ol and moves focus to the first one added. The button is outside the ol.
  • When an event is added while the reader watches, announce it from a role="status" element in the view, not from the list.
  • The timeline has no controls of its own and needs no script.
